project.title: Evaluation Metrics and Rewards for AI-Based Telescope Schedulers
project.goal: Quantitative metrics that summarize the goodness of a telescope observation schedule, validated on real DES data, packaged for the group toolkit.
project.phase: v0.1 — foundations: t_eff reconstructed, calibrated and validated; blur metric decomposed; per-night schedule scores on real DES nights

figures.title: Reconstructed vs pipeline t_eff
figures.caption: Our calibrated metric against DES's own quality pipeline across 74,323 exposures — log-correlation 0.952.

figures.title: The three factors of t_eff
figures.caption: Blur, cloud and sky terms as multipliers on exposure time.

figures.title: Fiducials rediscover physics
figures.caption: The per-band fiducial FWHM fit on data follows the atmospheric wavelength^-0.2 law.

figures.title: Delivered seeing by band
figures.caption: Blur distributions in each DECam filter; redder bands are sharper.

figures.title: Scheduler selection bias (Simpson's paradox)
figures.caption: Pooled, blur seems to improve with airmass — because the scheduler pointed low only in good seeing. Holding the night fixed recovers the physical X^0.6 trend. Evaluating schedulers from logged data is confounded by the logging policy.

figures.title: Seeing across the footprint
figures.caption: Median delivered FWHM over the DES footprint.

figures.title: Atmosphere vs scheduler
figures.caption: Zenith seeing (uncontrollable) vs delivered blur, and the t_eff fraction lost to pointing.

figures.title: Seeing seasonality
figures.caption: Monthly zenith seeing: Chilean summer delivers sharper images.

figures.title: Every night, scored
figures.caption: Composite schedule score for each DES night with a 60-day rolling median.

figures.title: The efficiency plane
figures.caption: Idle time vs poor conditions: two independent ways a night is lost.

figures.title: Best and worst nights
figures.caption: Exposure-by-exposure t_eff through the highest- and lowest-scoring nights.

figures.title: Keep-or-retake thresholds
figures.caption: Fraction of exposures meeting DES survey thresholds per band.

progress.milestone: t_eff physics identified from Terranova et al. + Neilsen et al. and mapped to the DES CSV columns
Empirical decomposition: blur x cloud core confirmed (log-corr 0.94), fiducials + sky term calibrated per band
skai_metrics package (data / teff / blur / schedule) + 4 validation tests passing on real data
Blur metric decomposed into atmosphere (uncontrollable) vs airmass (scheduler's choice)
Finding: scheduler selection bias inverts the blur-airmass law in pooled data (Simpson's paradox) — direct evidence that off-policy evaluation needs care
616 real DES nights scored with the composite schedule metric
Review composite-score weights with mentors; apply metrics to the group's prototype AI scheduler output
Integrate into the group's shared software toolkit
